market_analysis.market_type_reason: B2B: the buyers are data center owners and operators (enterprise, hyperscale, colocation, telecom).
market_analysis.market_definition: The Global Data Center Market covers dedicated data center facilities -- enterprise / captive, colocation, hyperscale / cloud and edge data centers -- and the technology, equipment, software and infrastructure installed in them. This landscape compares the TECHNOLOGY, EQUIPMENT, SOFTWARE AND INFRASTRUCTURE SOLUTION PROVIDERS that supply data centers. Hardware: servers (rack, blade, tower, mainframe, appliance), storage infrastructure (direct-attached, network-attached, storage area network, tape / optical / archival), network infrastructure (data center switches, routers, network interface cards and adapters, application delivery controllers and load balancers, network security appliances, structured copper and fiber cabling and connectivity, data center interconnect and other networking devices), power infrastructure (UPS systems, power distribution units, switchgear, transfer switches, transformers, backup generators, battery energy storage systems, busways and remote power panels), cooling infrastructure (IT-space air cooling, IT-space liquid cooling, chillers, cooling towers and dry coolers, coolant distribution units and fluid distribution, pumps, heat exchangers and cooling controls), rack and enclosure infrastructure (racks, cabinets and enclosures, hot- and cold-aisle containment, rack cable management and accessories), fire and life-safety infrastructure (fire and smoke detection, fire suppression, water and leak detection, emergency alarms, emergency power-off) and physical security infrastructure (access control, video surveillance, intrusion and perimeter detection, biometrics). Software: data center infrastructure management (DCIM), building and facility management, energy and power management, environmental and thermal management, digital twin and capacity planning, predictive maintenance, analytics and automation, and sustainability and carbon management software. Served data center types: enterprise and institutional, hyperscale and cloud, retail and wholesale colocation, telecom and network operator and other data centers, of every IT load capacity, across IT and telecom, BFSI, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, energy, government, media, education and transport. Geography: global (North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, Middle East & Africa).
market_analysis.core_scope: A core player itself makes or develops, and sells under its own name, data center hardware (servers, storage, networking, power, cooling, racks and enclosures, fire / life-safety or physical-security equipment) or data center infrastructure software (DCIM, BMS, energy, thermal, digital twin, predictive analytics, sustainability) for dedicated data centers -- including diversified technology and industrial groups for which data center products are one product line.
adjacent_segments: Data center engineering, design, construction and commissioning service providers (EPC and contractors)
Cloud and hyperscale data center owners and operators (cloud service providers)
Colocation, wholesale, edge and telecom data center owners and operators
Pure installation, integration, maintenance, managed-service and migration service firms with no own products
Distributors, value-added resellers and traders of other companies' equipment or software
Products for general commercial buildings, telecom towers or network switching sites that are not sold for dedicated data centers
Pure semiconductor component or raw-material suppliers that do not sell data center equipment or systems
